examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: Declinable neuter noun meaning 'dish', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.
Secondary conversational sense ('platter') (large flat serving dish) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Настоящий повар чувствует каждый вкус блюда.
examples.trans: A real chef feels every taste of the dish.

examples.text: Осталось ровно три минуты до готовности блюда.
examples.trans: Exactly three minutes remain until the dish is ready.
The chef prepared a delicious dish.

meanings.note: the present tense is normally left out: я мэр = I am the mayor
Present есть; у меня есть = I have. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to be; there is'.
future: буду / будешь ... + infinitive

examples.trans: You will be asking for forgiveness.

meanings.note: Prefix 'вы-' ('out of') marks outward movement or thorough completion (stem 'глядеть'). Used as an verbal verb meaning 'to look, appear'.

examples.trans: On top the costume looks simply super!

examples.text: Не говорите так, вы прекрасно выглядите!
examples.trans: Do not say that, you look wonderful!

meanings.note: Declinable masculine noun meaning 'hands', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.text: Денис, откуда у тебя в руках живой голубь?
examples.trans: Denis, where did you get a live pigeon in your hands?

examples.text: Так, друзья, где мой голубь по-дижонски?
examples.trans: All right, folks, where is my Dijon squab?

examples.text: Откуда под крышкой взялся этот живой голубь?
examples.trans: Where did that live pigeon under the cover come from?

meanings.note: Declinable feminine noun meaning 'restaurant', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.text: Разве в нашем ресторане гости едят голубей?
examples.trans: Do guests really eat pigeons in our restaurant?

examples.text: Нет, только не трогай этих дорогих голубей!
examples.trans: No, just do not touch those expensive pigeons!

examples.text: Пожалуйста, отдай мне хотя бы одного голубя!
examples.trans: Please give me back at least one pigeon!

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to cook; to prepare', paired with 'приготовить'.
Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to cook; to prepare', paired with 'приготовить'.

examples.text: Я уже не могу готовить, стирать, убирать. Я хочу на море!
examples.trans: I can't take the cooking, washing and cleaning any more. I want to go to the sea!

meanings.note: emphatic at the start of a sentence
Disbelief. Core Russian part meaning 'yes' in everyday speech.
Core Russian part meaning 'even' in everyday speech.
Дай! = give (me)!. Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to give', paired with 'давать'.

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: 'два' with masculine/neuter nouns, 'две' with feminine; the noun goes into the genitive singular

examples.text: Я выйду отсюда через две недели. Я решу все ваши проблемы.
examples.trans: I'll be out of here in two weeks. I'll solve all your problems.

meanings.note: думать о + prepositional = to think about

examples.trans: I have no time to think about that.

examples.text: Мне некогда об этом думать. Слишком много дел.
examples.trans: I have no time to think about that. There's too much to do.

meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'казать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to order', paired with 'заказывать'.

examples.text: Если опоздают, пицца бесплатно. Может, закажем?
examples.trans: If they're late, the pizza is free. Maybe we should order?

meanings.note: In the sky. Common feminine noun meaning 'star; celebrity' in everyday Russian.
Common feminine noun meaning 'star; celebrity' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: There are bright stars in the sky.

examples.text: Вот молодёжь, ничего не знают! Это же Лещенко! Звезда!
examples.trans: Young people these days, they don't know anything! That's Leshchenko! A star!

meanings.note: emphasis: вот поэтому ты и... = that's exactly why you...

examples.trans: I was born and grew up here.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: играть в + accusative (a game/sport)

examples.text: Напиши: трус не играет в хоккей.
examples.trans: Write: a coward doesn't play hockey.
The children are playing in the courtyard.

examples.text: Хорошая фотография! Напиши: трус не играет в хоккей.
examples.trans: Good photo! Write: a coward doesn't play hockey.

meanings.note: + genitive: 'из мэрии' = from the town hall

examples.text: Марина Сергеевна, я уже знаю. Мне звонили из мэрии.
examples.trans: Marina Sergeyevna, I already know. The town hall called me.

meanings.note: From Latin 'inspector' (observer, overseer, from 'inspicere', to look into).

examples.text: Инспекторы ищут нарушения только ради денег.
examples.trans: Inspectors look for violations only for money.
The inspector is checking the kitchen.

meanings.note: Something that happened. Prefix 'ис-' ('out from within') marks extraction or exhaustion (stem 'тория'). Common feminine noun meaning 'history; story' in everyday Russian.
Something that happened. Prefix 'ис-' ('out from within') marks extraction or exhaustion (stem 'тория'). Common feminine noun meaning 'history; story' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Этого не может быть. Это наша история.
examples.trans: That can't be. It's our history.

meanings.note: Question word. Core Russian adv meaning 'how; as' in everyday speech.
Как вы знаете = as you know. Core Russian adv meaning 'how; as' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: нас = us (gen/acc/prep); у нас = we have, at our place

meanings.en: other forms: нас (gen/acc), нам (dat), нами (instr), нас (prep)
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'we' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!

meanings.note: + prepositional: на сайте. Core Russian prep meaning 'on, onto; for' in everyday speech.
+ accusative: на второй срок. Core Russian prep meaning 'on, onto; for' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: The programme is on the website.
He is running for a second term.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'чинать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to begin, to start', paired with 'начать'.

examples.text: Аркаш, ну что скажешь? Когда начинать?
examples.trans: Arkasha, so what do you say? When do I start?

meanings.note: end-stressed in all oblique forms: ножа, ножом

examples.trans: Cutting a living person with a knife!
There is a sharp knife on the table.

examples.text: Нина, ну как ты могла? Живого человека ножом резать!
examples.trans: Nina, how could you? Cutting a living person with a knife!

meanings.note: accusative/genitive его (него after prepositions), dative ему (нему)
For masculine and neuter things. Core Russian pron meaning 'he; it' in everyday speech.

meanings.en: other forms: его (gen/acc), ему (dat), им (instr), нём (prep)
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'he; it' in everyday speech.
Formed with a diminutive/expressive Slavic suffix adding warmth or small scale. Common feminine noun meaning 'daddy; folder' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Now Daddy will handle this himself.

examples.text: На нашей кухне уже есть новая папочка.
examples.trans: In our kitchen there is already a new daddy.

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.
Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Послушайте, а можно в другое место? Здесь плохо пахнет.
examples.trans: Listen, could we go somewhere else? It smells bad in here.

подходить.gloss: to approach, to come up; to suit

meanings.note: очередь подходит = one's turn is coming up

Это мне подходит = that suits me. Prefix 'под-' ('under, up to') indicates approaching or supporting from below (stem 'ходить'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to approach, to come up; to suit', paired with 'подойти'.

examples.trans: Let's go, our turn in the queue is coming up.
The train is approaching the station.

examples.text: Я к печке подхожу. А он маячит перед глазами!
examples.trans: I walk up to the stove. And it dangles right before my eyes!

meanings.note: Informal. Core Russian interj meaning 'bye' in everyday speech.
As an adverb. Core Russian interj meaning 'bye' in everyday speech.

Completed: the job gets done. Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'мыть'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to wash', paired with 'мыть'.

meanings.en: to have a look, to take a look
meanings.note: One completed look. Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'смотреть'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to have a look', paired with 'смотреть'.
Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'смотреть'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to have a look', paired with 'смотреть'.

examples.trans: Can I go and have a look?

meanings.note: usually short form похож/похожа/похожи + на + accusative

examples.trans: He looks very much like his father.

examples.text: Нормально у вас тут, просторно. И маскировка хорошая, на дворников похожи.
examples.trans: It's nice in here, roomy. And good disguises—you look like janitors.

meanings.note: Asks about the reason. Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'чему').

examples.trans: Why are we going so slowly?

examples.text: Виталик, почему мы так медленно едем? Быстрее!
examples.trans: Vitalik, why are we going so slowly? Faster!

meanings.note: Short form: ты прав = you're right. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('right (side)').
Short form: ты прав = you're right. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('right (side)').

examples.text: Заходите. Поставьте, пожалуйста, правую ногу на кровать.
examples.trans: Come in. Please put your right foot on the bed.

приготовить.gloss: to prepare, to cook, to make

meanings.en: to cook, to make (food), to prepare
meanings.note: Takes accusative. Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'готовить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to prepare, to cook, to make', paired with 'готовить'.

examples.text: Я торт приготовила. Ты любишь сладкое?
examples.trans: I made a cake. Do you have a sweet tooth?

meanings.note: Animal or food. Common feminine noun meaning 'fish' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: A big platter of fish and crabs.

examples.text: На ужин мы приготовили свежую рыбу.
examples.trans: For dinner we cooked fresh fish.

examples.text: У нас есть большая тарелка рыбы и крабов.
examples.trans: We have a big platter of fish and crabs.

meanings.note: Сам, сама, само, сами. Core Russian pron meaning 'oneself (myself, yourself...)' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Я и сама хорошо проведу время.
examples.trans: I'll have a good time on my own.

meanings.note: The г sounds like в. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'егодня').

examples.text: Виктор Степанович, сегодня никак не могу.
examples.trans: Viktor Stepanovich, I really can't today.

meanings.note: 'сейчас буду' = I'll be right there
Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'ейчас').

examples.text: Конечно, помогу. Кто у вас сейчас начальник?
examples.trans: Of course I'll help. Who's your boss now?

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'пуститься'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to come downstairs'.

examples.trans: They are too lazy to come down to the restaurant!

examples.text: Надо всё сделать и спуститься вовремя.
examples.trans: We need to do everything and to come downstairs on time.

related.gloss: not to to come downstairs (negated infinitive)

meanings.note: Of things and people. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'тарый'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('old').
'старый друг' = an old friend. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'тарый'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('old').

examples.text: Славик, смотри сюда. Меняю свой новый айфон на твой старый телефон.
examples.trans: Slavik, look here. I'll swap my new iPhone for your old phone.

meanings.note: + instrumental: стал сентиментальным

+ infinitive. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'тать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to become', paired with 'становиться'.

examples.text: Ты слишком сентиментальным стал. А лидер должен быть жёстким.
examples.trans: You've become too sentimental. And a leader has to be tough.

творить.gloss: to do, to perpetrate; to create

meanings.en: to do, to get up to (something outrageous)
meanings.note: colloquial: что вы творите? = what are you doing?
Elevated. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to do, to perpetrate; to create', paired with 'сотворить'.

examples.text: Он сам не понимает, что творит.
examples.trans: He doesn't know what he is doing himself.

examples.text: Самсоновы, вы что творите? Хватит, я прошу вас!
examples.trans: Samsonovs, what are you doing? Stop it, I beg you!

meanings.note: Core Russian adv meaning 'too, also' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Мы же здесь выросли. И о людях тоже надо думать.
examples.trans: After all, we grew up here. And you have to think about people too.

meanings.note: softens a request: только не сердись = just don't be angry
One person, informal. Core Russian pron meaning 'you (informal)' in everyday speech.

meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'you (informal)' in everyday speech.

meanings.note: Declinable neuter noun meaning 'fillet', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.trans: The main thing is do not overcook this tender fillet.

examples.text: Сначала удалить хребет и охладить филе?
examples.trans: First remove the backbone and chill the fillet?

meanings.note: short form чисто: всё чисто = everything is clean
Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('clean').

examples.text: Нин, я всё помыл. Всё чисто.
examples.trans: Nina, I washed everything. It's all clean.

Conjunction. Core Russian pron meaning 'what' in everyday speech.
Core Russian pron meaning 'what' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Шикарно, скажите, сколько я вам за него должен?
examples.trans: Splendid, tell me, how much do I owe you for it?

examples.text: Костя сказал это совершенно шикарно и спокойно.
examples.trans: Kostya said this quite splendidly and calmly.
